title: Payment Arrangements Desk Guide — The Re-dating Lead and the Plan's Payment Record
content:
On a plan under Payment Arrangements, the re-dating lead given to a returned installment follows the plan's own payment record.

## Rule

The kept installment payments are the installment payments received under the plan less those returned — the number of installment payment entries on the plan's installment history less the number of returned installment payment entries.

- A plan with at least 6 kept installment payments and no returned installment payment in the last twelve months other than the most recent one takes a re-dating lead of 3 days.
- A plan with at least 6 kept installment payments and at least one other returned installment payment in the last twelve months takes a re-dating lead of 5 days.
- A plan with fewer than 6 kept installment payments takes a re-dating lead of 7 days.

Periods of twelve months are counted in whole months back from the handling date. The most recent returned installment payment is never counted as an "other" return.

## Decision table

| Kept installment payments | Other returned installment payments in the last 12 months | Re-dating lead |
|---|---|---|
| 6 or more | None | 3 days |
| 6 or more | One or more | 5 days |
| 5 or fewer | Any | 7 days |

## Questions answered by the rule

**A plan has received 9 installment payments and 2 of them were returned. Which row applies?**
9 less 2 leaves 7 kept installment payments, which is at least 6. If the only return in the last twelve months is the most recent one, the lead is 3 days; if the earlier return also falls within the last twelve months, the lead is 5 days. (Hypothetical figures.)

**A plan has 6 payments received and 1 returned.**
6 less 1 leaves 5 kept installment payments, fewer than 6: the lead is 7 days whatever the return history.

**Exactly 6 kept installment payments?**
6 meets "at least 6"; the lead is then 3 or 5 days according to the other returns.
